properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 23 at 4:02PM HST until November 25 at 6:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
...HIGH SURF WARNING IN EFFECT FOR NORTH AND WEST FACING SHORES
OF NIIHAU KAUAI OAHU MOLOKAI BIG ISLAND AND EAST FACING SHORES OF
OAHU...

.A large to extra large, long-period north- northwest swell build
down the island chain on Tuesday. While the source low aimed its
peak swell energy northeast of the area, enough was aimed at
Hawaii to see surf build to warning levels during the day on
Tuesday before subsiding on Wednesday ahead of an even larger
north-northwest swell on Wednesday night into Thursday.

* WHAT...Surf heights of 20 to 30 feet along north-facing shores,
12 to 16 feet along west-facing shores, and 8 to 12 feet along
Oahu's east-facing shores.

* WHERE...North and west facing shores of Niihau, Kauai, Oahu,
Molokai, Maui and the Big Island and east facing shores of Oahu.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Tuesday to 6 AM HST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...High. Expect very strong breaking waves and powerful
currents. Waves breaking in channel entrances may make
navigating the channels dangerous.
properties.instruction:
Stay away from the shoreline along the affected coasts. Be
prepared for road closures. Postpone entering or leaving channels
affected by the high surf until the surf subsides.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
will cause major flooding in low lying areas mainly around
Humboldt Bay. Up to 3 of saltwater inundation above ground level
is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways. Between 10.3 and 11.0 feet MLLW at the North Spit
tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal Flood Watch, High
astronomical tides and large surf may cause major flooding in
low lying areas along the Redwood Coast. Up to 2.5 foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 1 PM PST
Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday morning
through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 11:09 AM on
Wednesday and 11:56 AM on Thursday at the Humboldt Bay North
Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2
hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways and
houses in King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms. This may also
include highway 101 near College of the Redwoods and Hwy 255
near the Mad River Slough. Shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this are expected to
exceed the water levels seen in January of 2026 that caused
significant flooding in King Salmon.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
will cause major flooding in low lying areas mainly around
Humboldt Bay. Up to 3 of saltwater inundation above ground level
is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways. Between 10.3 and 11.0 feet MLLW at the North Spit
tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal Flood Watch, High
astronomical tides and large surf may cause major flooding in
low lying areas along the Redwood Coast. Up to 2.5 foot of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 1 PM PST
Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday morning
through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 11:09 AM on
Wednesday and 11:56 AM on Thursday at the Humboldt Bay North
Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2
hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways and
houses in King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms. This may also
include highway 101 near College of the Redwoods and Hwy 255
near the Mad River Slough. Shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this are expected to
exceed the water levels seen in January of 2026 that caused
significant flooding in King Salmon.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

the combined hazard significantly on Wednesday. These
predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that will enhance the
astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90
minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through
the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
